([[Chicago Heights, Illinois]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2014–2016) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2016]]) * [[Bob Cousy Award]] (2016) * [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] ([[2015–16 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2016]]) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Defensive Player of the Year (2016) * First-team All-SEC (2016) * SEC All-Freshman Team ([[2014–15 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2015]]) * [[SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|SEC Tournament]] MVP ([[2016 SEC Men's Basketball Tournament|2016]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2014) * ''[[USA Today|USAT]]'' All-USA (2014) * First team All-state (2013) | medal_templates = }} '''Tyler Ulis''' (born January 5, 1996) is an American [[college basketball]] player who is recently completed his college career for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] as a member of the [[2015–16 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2015–16 team]]. At Kentucky in 2015, he led his team in [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], he made the 2015 SEC All-Freshman Team and led the [[2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|2014–15 Kentucky team]] that won its first 38 games before losing to [[2014–15 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the final four of the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. As a sophomore, Ulis was a [[2016 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|Consensus first team All-American]] and earned the [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] and the Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year recognition. He played for [[Marian Catholic High School]] in [[Chicago Heights, Illinois]]. He was selected to play in both the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2014 McDonald's All-American Game]] and the 2014 [[Jordan Brand Classic]]. As a high school junior, he was a first team All-state selection, but he was overlooked by most top scouts until after his junior year of high school due to his height. ==Early life== Ulis was born in [[Southfield, Michigan]], and lived in [[Lima, Ohio]], with his mother. He ran track as a youth, competing in the [[800 metres|800 meters]] and [[1500 metres|1500 meters]]. He trained for basketball with his cousin and 2009 [[Big Ten Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year [[Travis Walton (basketball)|Travis Walton]]. Another of his cousins was Shareese Ulis, point guard for [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati Lady Bearcats]], who had been a two-time ''[[Toledo Blade]]'' Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-01-12/sports/ct-spt-0113-prep-bkb-athlete-of-month-20130112_1_preps-plus-athlete-tracy-abrams-tribune-wgn-ch|title=Tribune/WGN-Ch. 9 Athlete of the Month - Marian Catholic's Tyler Ulis|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-01-12|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Narang, Bob}} ==High school career== For high school Ulis moved to [[Matteson, Illinois]], where he lived with his father, James. In Ohio, he had been used to winning a high percentage of his games. When he arrived at Marian Catholic, he started his first game as a freshman against future [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball]] starting guard [[Tracy Abrams]]. He did not initially enjoy team success. As a freshman he was {{convert|5|ft|3|in|m|2}} tall and was being recruited by opposing high schools. He reached {{convert|5|ft|8|in|m|2}} by late in his sophomore year and began being recruited by college basketball teams.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-02-02/sports/ct-spt-0203-prep-bkb-spotlight-20120202_1_boys-basketball-school-freshman-last-winter|title=Boys basketball - Spotlight on Marian Catholic's Tyler Ulis|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2012-02-02|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} By the beginning of his junior season, Marian Catholic was regarded as a serious contender thanks to Ulis.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2012-11-21/sports/ct-spt-1122-prep-bkb-pvw-top-5-conferences-20121121_1_jahlil-okafor-tyler-ulis-boys-basketball|title=Boys basketball - Top 5 conferences at a glance|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2012-11-21|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} Because of his height, Ulis was overlooked until well into the recruiting process for top basketball schools. He was not highly recruited until his 2013–14 senior year of high school. Among schools regarded as high-major programs, only [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] and [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] made him offers during his junior year.{{cite web|url=http://www.highschoolcubenews.com/news_article/show/344112?referrer_id=599124|title=Henricksen: Okafor, Alexander and Ulis took different paths to McDonald's game|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2014-01-29|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe}} His other offers were from [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]], [[Colorado State Rams men's basketball|Colorado State]], [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola]], [[Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball|Northern Illinois]] and [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]].{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-01-31/sports/ct-spt-0201-prep-bkb-helfgot-blog-20130131_1_tyler-ulis-james-ulis-tom-izzo|title=Boys hoops blog - Ulis stands pat as stock soars|accessdate=2014-02-01|date=2013-01-31|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} During his junior season, his stock soared and Marian Catholic started winning. In the March 2013 [[Illinois High School Association]] Class 4A sectional round, Marian Catholic vied against [[Bloom High School]] and then played [[Edwardsville High School]] in the supersectional round.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-08/sports/ct-spt-0308-prep-bkb-helfgot-blog-20130308_1_simeon-niles-north-billy-voitik|title=Boys hoops blog - Helfgot tackles sectional final exams|accessdate=2014-02-01|date=2013-03-08|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-11/sports/ct-spt-0312-prep-bkb-helfgot-blog-20130311_1_1-simeon-proviso-west-tournament-jontrell-walker|title=Boys hoops blog - Helfgot breaks down supersectionals, picks winners|accessdate=2014-02-01|date=2013-03-11|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} Although Marian lost to a much taller Edwardsville team, it established a school record for wins with a 29–4 record and it won its IHSA sectional for the first time.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-12/sports/ct-spt-0313-prep-bkb-4a-marian-catholic-edwardsvil-20130312_1_marian-coach-mike-taylor-tyler-ulis-ki-jana-crawford|title=Boys hoops - 4A supersectional: Edwardsville too tall a task for Marian|accessdate=2014-02-01|date=2013-03-12|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Liesse, Bill}} Ulis finished fourth in the [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] balloting behind [[Jabari Parker]], [[Jahlil Okafor]] and Malcolm Hill.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-25/sports/ct-spt-0326-prep-bkb-gbk-mr-ms-basketball-announce-20130325_1_jabari-parker-tyra-buss-emmonnie-henderson|title=Mount Carmel's Buss, Simeon's Parker win Ms., Mr. Basketball|accessdate=2014-02-01|date=2013-03-25|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]}} He was a first team All-state selection by the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' along with Parker, Okafor, [[Cliff Alexander]] and [[Jalen Brunson]].{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-03-30/sports/ct-spt-0331-prep-bkb-all-state-first-team-20130330_1_jabari-parker-argo-sectional-team-usa|title=2013 Tribune All-State first team|accessdate=2014-02-01|date=2013-03-30|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} {{quote box|width=34em|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|align=left|quote="[Kentucky made the list because] of the success they have had there recently...John Calipari has produced the most point guards in recent years and has taken them right to the NBA. He obviously knows how to coach point guards. He knows how to put them in positions to lead the team. He’s a tough coach. There’s accountability from Day 1 to win and win at a high level."|source=—Ulis' father, James Ulis}} By August 8, 2013 when he was ranked as the 38th best prospect in the national class of 2014 and its 8th best point guard by [[ESPN]], he had several offers and named Iowa, Kentucky (although he did not have an offer from them at the time), [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] as his finalists (eliminating DePaul, [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] and [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]]).{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/chicago/high-school/post/_/id/3526/marian-catholics-ulis-trims-list-to-4-schools|title=Marian Catholic's Ulis trims list to 4 schools|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-08-08|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Powers, Scott}} Walton had played for Michigan State. He received an official offer from Kentucky on August 16.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/chicago/high-school/post/_/id/3541/ulis-receives-kentucky-offer|title=Ulis receives Kentucky offer|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-08-16|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Powers, Scott}} In early September, Ulis announced that he would not take an official visit to USC and had eliminated them from consideration.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/blog/chicago/colleges/post/_/id/9691/pg-ulis-down-to-3-after-eliminating-usc|title=PG Ulis down to 3 after eliminating USC|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-09-03|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Powers, Scott}} On September 13, Ulis committed to Kentucky.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-09-13/sports/chi-prep-boys-hoops-marian-catholics-tyler-ulis-picks-20130913_1_tyler-ulis-marian-catholic-boys-hoops|title=Boys hoops - Marian Catholic's Tyler Ulis picks Kentucky|accessdate=2013-10-14|date=2013-09-13|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Stainbrook, Michael}}{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2013/09/kentucky-lands-four-star-pg-tyler-ulis/|title=Kentucky Lands Four-Star PG Tyler Ulis|accessdate=2013-10-14|date=2013-09-14|work=[[SLAM Magazine]]}} Subsequently, [[Tyus Jones]] canceled his September 27–29 official visit to Kentucky.{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/blogs/225389792.html|title=Tyus Jones cancels Kentucky visit + Gophers recruiting notes|accessdate=2013-10-14|date=2013-09-26|work=[[Star Tribune]]|author=Rayno, Amelia}} Ulis entered his senior season as one of the five favorites to win Illinois Mr. Basketball (along with Okafor, Alexander, Brunson and [[Keita Bates-Diop]]).{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-11-27/sports/ct-spt-1128-prep-bkb-season-pvw-top-5-mr-basketbal-20131127_1_tyler-ulis-stevenson-brunson-boys-hoops|title=Boys hoops - Top 5 Mr. Basketball candidates|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-11-27|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} On December 7, 2013 at the [[UIC Pavilion]] in the Chicago Elite Classic, Ulis and Marion suffered one of their only two regular season losses to USC-bound guard [[Jordan McLaughlin]] and [[Etiwanda High School]], which was ranked number 6 nationally by ''[[USA Today]]''. Ulis had 30 [[point (basketball)|points]], 7 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 5 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]].{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2013-12-07/sports/ct-spt-1208-prep-bkb-elite-classic-rup-20131207_1_tyler-ulis-sean-o-mara-kentucky-bound-ulis|title=Boys hoops - Young falls to St. John Bosco at Elite Classic|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-12-07|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}{{cite web|url=http://articles.latimes.com/2013/dec/07/sports/la-sp-vi-boys-basketball-etiwanda-wins-in-chicago-to-improve-to-50-20131207|title=Boys' basketball: Etiwanda wins in Chicago to improve to 5-0 [Updated]|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2013-12-07|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|author=Sondheimer, Eric}} The January 25, 2014, matchup against junior Brunson and [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson High School]] was widely anticipated in the local press as the matchup of the two best point guards in the state.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2014-01-23/sports/chi-boys-basketball-blog-tyler-ulis-jalen-brunson--20140123_1_tyler-ulis-jalen-brunson-cliff-alexander|title=Boys hoops blog - Tyler Ulis, Jalen Brunson matchup should be a blast|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2014-01-23|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}}{{cite web|url=http://www.highschoolcubenews.com/news_article/show/342394?referrer_id=599124|title=Henricksen: Tyler Ulis vs. Jalen Brunson|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2014-01-24|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe}} Stevenson won as Brunson had 32 points on 9-for-15 [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]] shooting and an 11-for-14 [[free throw]] performance. Ulis had 23 points and 9 assists, including 18 points and 3 assists in the final eight minutes, but was only 5-for-20 from the field for the game.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2014-01-25/sports/chi-jalen-brunson-stevenson-top-tyler-ulis-marian--20140125_1_connor-cashaw-jalen-brunson-terrone-parham|title=Boys hoops - Jalen Brunson, Stevenson hold off Marian Catholic|accessdate=2014-01-31|date=2014-01-25|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} Ulis posted a career-high 42 points on February 22 against [[Lake Forest High School (Illinois)|Lake Forest High School]] to go along with 6 [[steal (basketball)|steals]], 6 rebounds and 5 assists.{{cite web|url=http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2014-02-22/sports/chi-tyler-ulis-evan-boudreaux-marian-catholic-lake-20140222_1_tyler-ulis-ki-jana-crawford-jalen-brunson|title=Boys hoops - Tyler Ulis outdoes Evan Boudreaux as Marian tops Lake Forest|accessdate=2014-02-24|date=2014-02-23|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike}} During his senior year, Marian was the number 1 seed in the [[Thornton Township High School|Thornton]] sectional of the IHSA Class 4A tournament. On March 11, Ulis had 40 points to lead Marian past [[Bloom High School]] 66–45. In the game, which was a rematch from the prior year, he made his first six shots, all three-pointers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nwitimes.com/sports/high-school/illinois/bloom-no-match-for-ulis-marian/article_1aca9fa6-3643-5a3e-bd8f-43db6eca45ee.html|title=Bloom no match for Ulis, Marian|accessdate=2014-03-13|date=2014-03-11|work=[[The Times of Northwest Indiana]]|author=Arvia, Phil}}{{cite web|url=http://southtownstar.suntimes.com/sports/26142250-419/boys-basketball-ulis-three-mendous-in-marian-catholics-win-over-bloom.html|title=Boys Basketball: Ulis three-mendous in Marian Catholic’s win over Bloom|accessdate=2014-03-15|date=2014-03-11|work=[[SouthtownStar]]|author=Disabato, Pat}} On March 18, Marian lost its supersectional rematch against Edwardsville in [[overtime (sports)|overtime]], again falling one game short of reaching the final four in [[Peoria, Illinois]] and finishing with a 28–3 record. During the 2016 [[NBA Draft Combine]], Ulis was not only the second-shortest player to participate in the event (behind only [[Kahlil Felder]], who measured at 5'9.5" as opposed to 5'10"), but he was also the lightest recorded player in draft combine history at 149 pounds.https://mediacentral.nba.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/53/2016/05/2016-Draft-Combine-Anthropometric-Results.pdf?cid=nbacomsocial_tw_sf26163323 Furthermore, about two weeks before the draft began, it was revealed that Ulis had a problem with his hip that may one day require surgery.
